PR Summary by Qodo

Add Save all for received files (test PR; do not merge) ✨ Enhancement 🧪 Tests 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Add one-tap saving of received files through one share sheet or spaced downloads.
>• Skip files already saved, and leave cancelled or failed shares available for another tap.
>• Add unit and two-browser coverage and document the behavior. Test PR; do not merge.
>
Merge Risk 🟢 Low

Blast radius 🟡 Medium 💥 2 capabilities

- 2 affected capabilities within one bounded functional scope: received-media-export. - This is one bounded browser integration for exporting files already received into the shared-space table. saveall.js selects files from the page's prints/files/incoming state and index.html supplies the single Save all entry point and browser handoff callbacks; these are implementation hops for the same user outcome, not separate capabilities. - This is a distinct user operation within the same received-media export integration: the user taps one received file and hands that file to the browser, rather than selecting a batch. - It shares the integration boundary and in-memory file state with Save all, but has a separate user-visible outcome and trigger.
Behavioral complexity 🟡 Medium 🧩 Interacting branches, Compatibility cases

- The changed correctness conditions are more than a direct transformation. - Before: there was no batch export state machine. - After: the implementation coordinates share-sheet success, cancellation, non-cancel failure, download fallback, per-file download exceptions, download spacing, busy re-entry, and the handed set. - Before: browser handoff mode did not need to be coordinated with later taps. - After: share support and prior share failure select different modes, and handed state must be updated only after a share succeeds or an individual download starts. - New correctness condition: these branches and transitions must preserve the invariant that a file remains retryable after cancellation/failure but is not handed over twice after successful export. - The compatibility case is the differing browser capabilities and share-sheet acceptance behavior; these use existing browser APIs but introduce new behavior across their success/failure modes.
Sources
[web/index.html\[335-343\]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/blob/941cf4f41d578799f686c69b049af3577995765d/web/index.html#L335-L343) ```html // Save all (F13): every received photo in one tap. The share sheet once with all of them, or downloads const saveAll = createSaveAll({ batch: (handed) => saveBatch({ prints, files, incoming, me: id, handed }), canShare: (list) => !!navigator.share && !!navigator.canShare?.({ files: list }), share: (list) => navigator.share({ files: list }), download: downloadFile, toast, }); $('saveall').onclick = () => saveAll.tap(); ```
Potential damage 🟢 Low 🩹 Reversible

- If this capability regresses, a user may be unable to export some or all currently received files, may need to retry, or may see an incorrect duplicate-suppression result. - The source does not show persistent application-state mutation or an external side effect beyond the user's browser share/download action. - Files remain represented in the page's in-memory files map, so recovery is normally a later tap while the page and received files remain available; a browser-level download/share failure may still require user action. - This is a single end-to-end export capability within one bounded integration. - Revert restores the prior code path, but a failed or missed handoff is not automatically repaired. - The user can retry Save all while the page retains the received File objects; a successfully completed external download/share is not undone by code rollback.
Sources
[web/index.html\[335-343\]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/blob/941cf4f41d578799f686c69b049af3577995765d/web/index.html#L335-L343) ```html // Save all (F13): every received photo in one tap. The share sheet once with all of them, or downloads const saveAll = createSaveAll({ batch: (handed) => saveBatch({ prints, files, incoming, me: id, handed }), canShare: (list) => !!navigator.share && !!navigator.canShare?.({ files: list }), share: (list) => navigator.share({ files: list }), download: downloadFile, toast, }); $('saveall').onclick = () => saveAll.tap(); ```
Assessed commit 941cf4f
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD UI["Save all button"] --> Batch["Eligible files"] --> CanShare{"Share batch?"} -->|Yes| Share["Share sheet"] --> Handed["Handed IDs"] CanShare -->|No| Downloads["Spaced downloads"] --> Handed Single["Single-photo save"] --> Handed ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Package desktop files into one archive
- ➕ Avoids multiple browser download prompts and delays. - ➖ Requires archive creation and delivers an archive rather than individual files.
>**Recommendation:** Keep the current share-or-download approach for this feature: it preserves individual files and keeps share decisions testable outside the browser. An archive is worth considering only if desktop browsers consistently block the spaced downloads.

Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (6)
1. Mixed save taps can hand over duplicates 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>save(p) does not check whether Save all is busy or whether its PID is already handed over, while
>Save all continues through a snapshot of files taken before its download waits. Tapping a photo
>during a batch can download it immediately and again when the batch reaches it; a pending individual
>share can likewise overlap a Save all share.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/index.html[R327-328]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/142/files#diff-8f62b6ced28d3396b501d2e89a2e7cb761d16cd7dc977aebece03d4a5da5c24eR327-R328) > >```diff >+ if (navigator.canShare?.({ files: [file] })) navigator.share({ files: [file] }).then(() => saveAll.handed.add(p.pid), () => {}); >+ else { downloadFile(file); saveAll.handed.add(p.pid); } >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Individual photo saves can overlap a Save all operation and hand over a file twice, including after it was already saved by the batch. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/index.html[317-328] >- web/saveall.js[32-55] >## Recommended Fix >Coordinate the individual and batch paths through shared in-flight and handed state. Check that state before starting an individual handoff and again before each delayed batch download, while leaving the share call inside the initiating tap on iOS. Clear reservations when a share fails or is cancelled. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Blocked downloads disappear from retries 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>tap() marks a photo as handed over whenever downloadFile() returns, but that function only
>clicks an anchor and cannot establish that the browser accepted the download. If the browser blocks
>later files in a batch, the next tap excludes them and says there is nothing new to save.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[53]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/142/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR53-R53) > >```diff >+ try { download(ready[i].file); handed.add(ready[i].pid); } catch (e) { console.warn('download failed', ready[i].file?.name, e); } >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A browser can refuse automatic multiple downloads without throwing from an anchor click, yet Save all permanently excludes those files from retries. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[50-54] >- web/index.html[328-334] >## Recommended Fix >Use a desktop handoff whose acceptance can be established, or explicitly treat individual anchor-click outcomes as unknown rather than confirmed. Give the person a recoverable way to retry or handle browser download permissions; keep the original file bytes and do not persist received files. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Failed downloads go unreported to people 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>The batch download loop catches exceptions from download() but only sends them to console.warn.
>When an object URL cannot be created or an anchor click throws, the earlier “Downloading” toast
>remains the only user-facing result even though that photo was left for a retry.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[53]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/142/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR53-R53) > >```diff >+ try { download(ready[i].file); handed.add(ready[i].pid); } catch (e) { console.warn('download failed', ready[i].file?.name, e); } >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Synchronous batch download failures are logged but never shown to the person saving the photos. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[50-55] >## Recommended Fix >Count failed downloads and show a final toast stating how many could not be started and that another tap will retry them. Continue attempting the other files and leave failed PIDs out of the handed set. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

4. One failed share stops future share sheets 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>downloadNext becomes true after any non-cancellation share rejection and is never cleared after
>the fallback batch. Once a phone has used the prompted download fallback, later newly received
>photos also bypass its available share sheet for the rest of the tab session.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[R44-45]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/142/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR44-R45) > >```diff >+ downloadNext = true; >+ return toast('Couldn’t open the share sheet. Tap Save all again to download'); >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A transient share failure permanently changes Save all from sharing to downloading, even for photos received later. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[26-55] >## Recommended Fix >Make the download fallback apply to the explicitly requested next tap, then restore normal share eligibility for subsequent batches. Preserve the rule that a rejected share never starts downloads without another user tap. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/bcc6791a-736b-48e5-bab8-502cacaf0464?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/bcc6791a-736b-48e5-bab8-502cacaf0464)
5. A stuck share blocks later Save all taps 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>tap() keeps busy true until the promise from share(list) settles, with no recovery path if it
>never does. After a browser share operation remains pending, every later Save all tap returns “Still
>saving,” including taps for photos received afterward.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[R41-43]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/142/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR41-R43) > >```diff >+ if (sharing) { >+ try { await share(list); } catch (e) { >+ if (e?.name === 'AbortError') return; // cancelled: nothing happens, the photos stay available >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A share promise that does not settle leaves Save all permanently busy for the tab. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/saveall.js[32-55] >## Recommended Fix >Provide a bounded, user-visible recovery path for an unsettled share, with an operation token so a late settlement cannot mark a later batch as handed over or clear its busy state. Do not put an await before the initial navigator.share call or automatically download after a timeout. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/3024c0ce-6fd5-4c66-a6e2-9654e6b17ca4?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/3024c0ce-6fd5-4c66-a6e2-9654e6b17ca4)
6. Save all misses photos during verification 🐞 Bug
>
>Description >
> >
>saveBatch() sees a photo neither as ready nor as arriving between removal from incoming and
>insertion into files. The receive path awaits checksum verification during that interval, so a tap
>then reports “Nothing new to save” even though the full photo is finishing.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[web/saveall.js[R16-18]](https://github.com/jtbinith/qodo-hack-2026/pull/142/files#diff-1197fbbadbb14a53258dbd75d68b20c8bf37f2e49062120e60b6b11916a8861fR16-R18) > >```diff >+ let arriving = 0; >+ for (const fid of incoming.keys()) if (!fid.startsWith('thumb:') && !files.has(fid)) arriving++; >+ return { ready, arriving }; >``` >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A completed transfer vanishes from both Save all counts while its checksum is being verified. >## Fix Focus Areas >- web/index.html[205-231] >- web/saveall.js[10-18] >## Recommended Fix >Keep full-photo transfers represented as arriving until verification finishes and the verified File enters `files`, or track the verification phase separately and include it in Save all's arriving count. Do not hand over bytes before verification succeeds. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
